raw.cause: nav's handler sleeps 200 ms (COCKPIT_FAULT=slow-reply) between MsgReceive and MsgReply, so every display MsgSend stays REPLY-blocked for ~205 ms against a 50 ms budget. For example, receive at 2216.662 ms and reply at 2427.024 ms. The delay is inside nav's own handler, not scheduling: nav already runs at display's priority through priority inheritance, and the gps and logger calls are fast. The last request was still unanswered at trace end.
raw.qnx_call: MsgReply delayed in nav (nav_handle sleeps 200 ms before replying to display's MsgSend)
raw.fix_summary: Remove the blocking sleep from nav's request path so MsgReply goes out right after the gps lookup. If nav genuinely needs slow work, do it outside the receive/reply window: precompute the route in a worker thread and reply with the cached value. Don't raise the 50 ms budget to hide a deliberate 200 ms stall.
